title: Reverse large text efficiently with StringBuilder
answer: For an in-memory text block, a direct Java solution is `new StringBuilder(text).reverse().toString()`. `StringBuilder` stores mutable characters, `reverse()` reverses them efficiently, and `toString()` produces the final immutable String. AeroTopo's `SurveyAlgorithms.reverse` uses exactly this approach. Its time complexity is O(n) for n characters and it requires O(n) space for the mutable character storage/result. For extremely large content that cannot comfortably fit in memory, a streaming or chunked design would be needed instead.
